links.outcome: Concordance with expert consensus, agentic system vs simpler RAG and full-context baselines on same data
links.effect: Agentic 79.6% concordance vs iterative RAG 75.4% and full-context 75.8% (+3.8 and +4.2 pp; p = 0.006 and 0.007); iterative RAG and full-context did not differ (p = 1.00).
links.quote: The agentic system reached 79.6% concordance (95% CI 76.4-82.8), exceeding both baselines (+3.8 and +4.2 pp; p = 0.006 and 0.007).

links.outcome: Rate and clinical severity of system errors versus expert disagreement
links.effect: System error rate 12.2% vs expert disagreement 13.6%; 57.8% of system errors clinically significant vs 18.8% of expert disagreements.
links.quote: The system error rate (12.2%) was comparable to expert disagreement (13.6%), but severity was inverted: 57.8% of system errors were clinically significant versus 18.8% of expert disagreements.

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation comparing an agentic reasoning architecture against baseline RAG and full-context methods on clinical records; it evaluates model/agent architectures rather than an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
